correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed both 27-edge cubic graphs and enumerated all matchings without using the provided program as an oracle. Möbius: 36,627 nonempty simplices, critical cells one 0, twenty-three 5, one 6; 18,301 matching pairs, all 199,908 cover relations sorted. Prism: 36,625 nonempty, critical one 0, twenty-six 5, two 6; 18,298 pairs, all 199,890 covers sorted. Exact signed Morse boundaries independently reconstructed and matched all supplied JSON entries: Möbius 1x23 matrix with entry +1 at column 6; prism 2x26 matrix with determinant +1 on columns 8,14. Since maps of S5 to wedges of S5 are classified by degree, unimodular integer cancellations remove the sixth cells and yield wedges of 22 and 24 S5 integrally. No inference of homotopy from mod-two Betti alone.
residual_risks: This is exact for two 18-vertex graphs, not an all-width formula.
The independent reconstruction follows the signed cellular-Morse elimination recurrence; algorithmic correctness is justified by cancellation of acyclic face pairs.

value.rationale: The Möbius versus cylinder twist comparison is a natural controlled combinatorial change for cubic ladder families. Its nine-rung boundary fills the next omitted ordinary matching-complex case, proving exact integral homotopy and a nontrivial difference of two sphere generators where the preceding cases exhibit mixed dimensions. This is a motivated exact invariant, not an arbitrary small-slice number.
residual_risks: Does not establish a general width-periodicity law or equivariant structure.

final_claim: Ordinary matching complexes of the 18-vertex Möbius ladder M18 and nine-rung prism C9 square K2 are integrally wedges of 22 and 24 five-spheres, respectively.
